purpose: Estimate task-template variability and exercise the measurement protocol before any held-out comparison. These templates are not executed evidence.

order_randomization.method: For each task repetition, Fisher-Yates shuffle candidates in lock-file order using this Mulberry32 draw: x = (x + 0x6D2B79F5) >>> 0; t = Math.imul(x ^ (x >>> 15), x | 1); t ^= t + Math.imul(t ^ (t >>> 7), t | 61); return ((t ^ (t >>> 14)) >>> 0) / 4294967296.

preregistration.pairing: Same task state, model identifier/version, prompt budget, browser build, and time budget across available candidates; randomize candidate order within each task repetition.
preregistration.reset: Recreate each task's declared synthetic initial_state before every candidate run; capture reset evidence and reject contaminated starts.
preregistration.success_rule: Pass only when every success_predicate is independently read back from the resulting task state. Dispatch acknowledgments, tool claims, and success notifications alone do not pass.
preregistration.failure_rule: Timeout, unsupported operation, missing predicate evidence, contaminated reset, or incomplete cleanup is retained and reported; no post-run exclusions.
preregistration.analysis: Pilot estimates are descriptive. Report success counts and Wilson intervals, per-template paired log wall-time differences, median and range for cost measures, and design-review sample size separately. Do not claim a comparison win or infer held-out performance from this pilot.
preregistration.design_review_disclosure: Six pilot templates require human rubric review; report n=6 templates and n=18 planned task-runs separately from automated predicates.
preregistration.held_out_boundary: Pilot IDs P01-P30 are permanently excluded from the held-out set. Freeze held-out IDs, task rubric, baseline configurations, analysis code, and split digest before inspecting any pilot outcomes.
preregistration.safety: Use synthetic/local state only. Do not sign into personal accounts, send messages, submit forms to external services, or cause irreversible external effects.
